newsitem.title: USA: Frost hits northern Iowa, crop damage uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Frost hits northern Iowa, crop damage uncertain.

text.p: The first frost of the season occurred Saturday morning in parts of central and northern Iowa, but it was too early to assess the extent of damage to corn and soybeans, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Comments received by the Statistics Service regarding the corn and soybeans ranged from "look excellent" to "not as good as farmers thought."

Corn harvest began last week with less than one percent cut as of Sunday. Moisture of the early-harvested corn was in the upper 30 to low 40 percent range. Corn was 16 percent mature as of Sunday versus 40 percent last year and for the average.
Corn was rated 20 percent excellent, 51 good, 24 fair, four poor and one very poor.
About 48 percent of the soybeans had turned color versus 59 a year ago and the 60 percent average. Leaves were dropping on seven percent versus 19 a year ago and the 26 average.
In the southwest and south central districts beans "are setting a lot of pods with two beans as opposed to three beans per pod," the service said.
Soybeans were rated 16 percent excellent, 50 good, 27 fair, six poor and one very poor.
Topsoil moisture was rated three percent surplus, 58 adequate, 33 short and six very short.
